selected_result: Difference between true and computed least-squares residual norms for the normal equations method

bibliographic_source.title: Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms, 2nd ed., Chapter 20: The Least Squares Problem, Problem 20.6

paper_locations.anchor: Problem 20.6: the bound on |r^T r - rhat^T rhat| derived from (20.12) and (20.13)

task_clarification: Consider min_x ||b - A x||_2 with A in R^{m x n}. Let xhat be the computed LS solution from the normal equations method and x the exact solution.
Define rhat = b - A xhat and r = b - A x.
Formalize the bound |r^T r - rhat^T rhat| <= c_{m,n} u ||x - xhat||_2 ||A||_2 (||A||_2 ||xhat||_2 + ||b||_2) + O(u^2).
c_{m,n} is a modest constant depending only on m and n; u is the unit roundoff.
scope_constraints: The computed solution comes from the normal equations method, as in the source.
State the bound to first order in u, keeping the O(u^2) remainder explicit.
Exclude overflow and underflow consistently with the source model.
Represent the two residuals and the rounding assumptions rather than postulating the requested bound.
